text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after surging nearly 16% over two weeks, as the market digested a major shift in the diesel supply outlook. On October 9th, a Trump administration deal to import Russian diesel into U.S. and global markets became public—a direct threat to refiner margins, since refiners like Marathon profit most when they can sell fuel at high prices during tight supply. This announcement reversed the tailwind that had driven the stock up sharply: over the prior week, geopolitical tensions (Iran attacks on tankers, Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, and now Hurricane Isaias threatening Gulf production) had tightened global fuel supplies and pushed crude prices higher, creating a profitable environment for U.S. refiners.

The longer trend here is colliding supply shocks and policy response. The Middle East and Eastern Europe conflicts have already crippled refinery capacity worldwide, which is why crude and diesel prices have stayed elevated—but that same damage is making Trump willing to circumvent normal trade channels and add Russian supply. U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, and diesel and gasoline storage are both lean, so new supply entering the market could compress the prices refiners can charge even as global crude remains above $125 a barrel.
